licenses.note: The reference is Build Guide 0.4.9 at tag v0.4.9. Its repository, settings.gradle, mods.toml and fabric.mod.json all name CC BY-NC 3.0, and its top-level LICENSE is the only licence statement, so its icon and language files are covered by it too.

deviations.what: The five screens and their widget kinds are not implemented, so neither is the B key that opens the main screen, and the state is never saved: the reference writes the state file when a screen closes.
deviations.why: A mod cannot open a screen or draw a widget of its own yet, which is what #1760 gives it. The overlay draws the world and reads the three key binds, and the state and config codecs are in place for the screens to use once they exist, so the world draw is complete while the editing surface is not.

deviations.what: The state and config files live under the root File.open(r"files") answers, at buildguide/<world>@<dimension>.dat and config/buildguide.cfg, where the reference writes <gameDir>/buildguide/<world>@<dimension>.dat and <gameDir>/config/buildguide.cfg. The host also refuses a name that differs only in case from an entry that is already there, so two worlds whose names differ only in case share one guide here, where the reference on a case-sensitive filesystem kept two.
deviations.why: A mod may write only inside the directory #1757 gives it, so a guide the reference already saved at the game directory's path is not imported and a guide this port saves is not read by the reference. The file formats themselves are the reference's, byte for byte.

deviations.what: A state file whose number does not parse stops the load where it is and keeps what it already applied, where the reference lets the NumberFormatException escape getState() and the client fails the tick. Nothing clamps after a stopped load, so a truncated file can hold an iShapeSet past its shape sets.
deviations.why: grug has no exception to raise, and turning a stopped load into a fresh state is the overlay's to decide. The partial load is exactly what the reference applies before it throws.

deviations.what: The three config comments are the en_us sentences as fixed text, where the reference writes the client's language through Translatable, so a non-English client's rewritten config is not the reference's bytes.
deviations.why: mod_api.json has no entry for a translated string, so a translated comment needs a general host function that a port of any translated mod would use.

deviations.what: A catenary whose Newton solve does not converge draws no cells: the reference either reports an invalid value or never leaves its loop, and the port answers no cells at once in both cases.
deviations.why: grug cannot raise an error to the player yet. A solve whose values leave the finite range makes the reference throw, and a solve whose Newton step changes nothing (dx 1419, dz 0, an added length of 1) repeats that step until the shape is cancelled. The port ends the solve when a step is non-finite or changes nothing, which bounds both arms, and its cell loops keep the reference's own bounds rather than a cap of this port's own.

deviations.what: The state's depthTest flag is read from the file and written back, but every cube is drawn depth-tested against the world: the reference turns the depth test off for the whole guide when the flag is false, so a guide behind a hill becomes visible.
deviations.why: The world overlay's draw_triangle has one depth mode, the one that hides geometry behind blocks, and a per-draw or per-overlay depth-test switch is not part of it yet.

deviations.what: A shape is generated in render_world on the frame that draws it, where the reference generates it on a cached thread pool and keeps drawing the old buffer until the new one is ready. A large shape therefore stalls its frame here and appears complete at once, instead of appearing a few frames late.
deviations.why: grug has no thread to hand generation to, so a shape's update cannot run beside the frame. The asyncEnabled config option is read and written byte for byte but changes nothing yet.

deviations.what: The reference binds toggleEnable, setOrigin and setGlobalOrigin to GLFW_KEY_UNKNOWN, so they are unbound until the player sets them in Controls, and binds openBuildGuide to B. The port declares G, O and P as the defaults of toggle_enable, set_origin and set_global_origin, and has no binding for B.
deviations.why: A key has to have a one-character default in about.json, since the game's Controls screen cannot show an unbound mod binding, and the three ids are named after what they do rather than after the reference's key names.

deviations.what: The port keeps one state in memory and reloads that world@dimension's file when the key changes, where the reference keeps a state per key for the whole session, so revisiting a world there keeps the edits made in it.
deviations.why: Since this port never saves a state yet, the edits made in one world are lost when the overlay moves to another; a per-key store arrives with the save that makes them worth keeping.
